transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… people have been noticing I’m moving strangely. Sometimes I’m really slowed down, like it takes me too long to answer or even get up from a chair. Other times I’m just pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands, like I can’t shake something off. It’s been noticeable enough that I figured I should come in.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?
Yeah… sometimes. It’s mostly sounds. Like I’ll hear my old headset beep, or a supervisor kind of voice saying my name… or “too slow.” But my laptop’s closed, and there’s no phone ringing.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?
Not really… I don’t think so. I mean, my sleep’s not great sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel unusually energetic or like I don’t need it.
When you get very slowed down, do you ever find yourself stuck in one position for a long time?

Yeah… sort of. Not like I’m frozen for hours, but I’ll catch myself just standing there, like in the kitchen with my coffee halfway up, and I don’t really know how long I’ve been doing it. Or I’ll just keep walking the same little loop by the couch for no reason.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… most days, I guess. It’s kind of just there in the background most of the time — feeling down, guilty, not really interested in much. Some weeks are a little better, but it hasn’t really gone away. Sleep’s been part of it too.
Do the voices ever happen when you’re not feeling depressed?

Yeah… sometimes. There’ve been a few weeks where I felt more normal, like I was getting stuff done, but I’d still hear that supervisor voice, or feel like the old ticketing system was flagging me somehow.
Has there ever been a time when the voices lasted for at least 2 weeks while you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. There were a few weeks where my mood was more normal, like I was actually getting things done, but I still heard that supervisor voice… or felt like the old ticketing software was flagging me.
Have you taken any antipsychotic medicines recently?
I’m not really sure… I don’t think so recently, no.
Have you noticed a tremor in your hands when they’re resting?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed my hands shaking when I’m just sitting still.
Has there been a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… there’s been stretches like that. It’s been on and off, but mostly there for… about two years, I guess. A little over two years. It eases up sometimes, but not for long.
During those depressed stretches, did you ever feel hopeless nearly every day?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I wouldn’t say I thought about it that clearly every day. It was more just… feeling low and stuck, I guess.
Have the voices or the feeling that the old ticketing system was flagging you been going on for at least 6 months?
Yeah… it’s been longer than six months. Maybe around a year and a half, closer to two. And it wasn’t only when I was really depressed.
During those low periods, do you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess so. Stuff like sketching, or taking notes on coffee I try, even weekend hikes… I still start to do them sometimes, but it’s like there’s nothing there. I open the notebook or put my boots on and just… don’t feel drawn to it.
When someone else moves your arm or body into a position, does it tend to stay there for a while?

Not really like someone moves me and I stay that way. It’s more… when I’m overwhelmed, I’ll notice I’m just standing there with my mug halfway up, or pacing the same little loop by the couch. I don’t always realize right away.
Have there been times when you stopped speaking altogether, even though you were awake?
I don’t think so. I might get quiet, like… not want to answer, but I don’t remember being awake and just completely unable to talk.

Before the voices or the feeling that the ticketing system was flagging you ever started, had you already gone through a period of at least two weeks of feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… I think so. The low part was there before that, for a long time. Like, not just a week or two—more like couple years, with only short stretches where it let up a bit.
During those low periods, did you feel worthless nearly every day?

Yeah… I guess so. I’d get stuck replaying little mistakes from work, like a slow reply or something from a contract job, and it would feel like I’d let everyone down. Like maybe I deserved getting fired.
Looking back over the whole time you’ve been ill, have the voices been present during most of that time, including times when you were not depressed?

Yeah… I think so. There were a few stretches, like a couple weeks maybe, where my mood was more normal and I was getting stuff done, but I’d still hear that supervisor voice sometimes, or feel like the old ticketing system was flagging me.
Since these problems started, has your ability to work or take care of yourself gotten a lot worse?

Yeah… it has gotten worse. I mean, I’m still managing to keep a place and get by, but work’s been harder. I miss deadlines, avoid calls sometimes, and then I guess I come off unreliable.

And outside of work… I don’t see people as much. Basic stuff like meals, errands, even hiking, I kind of let slide unless I really push myself.
Looking back over the whole time you’ve been ill, have you been depressed for most of that time?

Yeah… I think most of the time, honestly. It’s not always as bad every week, but the sadness and guilt are kind of… there in the background. And I don’t get interested in much, or sleep right, even when it’s a lighter stretch.
